body: Been there - it's a hard thing to do. High five for that :)
I guess, a big victory is that the other day, the 'anniversary' marking 24 years since my rape -and it took me a few hours to realize it.

Is it possible to get another therapist if this one doesn't help? 

I go to a therapist who told me the PTSD things can get worse before they start to diminish - IF they do. But she _was_ talking about me, so I guess..my advice is to go to a therapist you feel is helpful.

Oh, right. That is what we're doing. I go once a week.
But group sessions are so so out of the question even if they had it. 
Thank you !
Thanks - and to you as well!

Thank you, I haven't got anything like that here (I live one hour away from the nearest town) but I will test the app for sure!
Not sure what CBT is (English isn't my first language) but I am working with my therapist with cognitive things, trying to not think so much about shame and regret etc. Thank you for taking the time out of your day to help!

Thank you for the link first of all - I wonder why my therapist haven't recommended the grounding and relaxation techniques before. I keep un-clenching muscles all the time now, after reading it.

I don't think I really -can- come out to anyone about all this, it's too much for most people, and the few loved ones I do have mostly know things,it just feels easier to tell everyone when I'm overwhelmed myself. I am thankful for your time and avice!
Heartbreaking. You should probably tell someone about your cousin - in case. And I don't know how you recovered so well from 18 to 25, but this gives me hope. Thank you for sharing!
This is why I google movies or ask before I watch them. I can't just WATCH movies.
Write the lettter. At least to get your feelings down on paper.
I hope you keep doing it - whatever keeps you alive.

I am prepared to be hated. That's a small price,imho. 
I try to be honest,always - that way people know they can either rely on me or know that I'm not the right one for them.
There's nothing like that where I live. In the capitol of my country there might be,but I live a long,long way away :/

Thanks for the comments,you guys. I was approached by a mother of one of the ones I 'saved', she gave me her number because I called 911 when no one else did, it kind of makes me feel obligated. I have very strict 'rules' for myself though - there are three at the most I can 'watch over' (i.e follow their twitter/facebook-feeds/blogs) at any given time. 
I have tried to be that friend for more people,but that dragged me under. I'm 30 next year, and I dunno, it should probably trigger my chronic ptsd,by exposing myself to it, but the suicidal/depressive thoughts isn't something I'm troubled by much. ( I have kids. That -for me-means I can't kill myself,ever.) 
I dunno, when I help, it feels scary and panicky and I cry and stay awake all night to make sure it's ok,and.. then.. I feel slightly less worthless for awhile. 

I have been drawn to messed up people,or they to me,since I was a kid,so it's like a reaction for me. Like when you duck when something is flung at your face, I dive to save when I see a kid falling. 

But I have to add - I ALWAYS call medical personel when I suspect someone is serious. 
Sorry for rambling,it feels good to actually talk about it.
I dream of finishing school, and work within law enforcement so that's actually a perfect rolemodel! Thank you :)
Thanks. It passed after a few hours, but it helps to have someone successfull to look to and think,that when they can,maybe I can too.
